Reconcile an income statement step by step

Source: R/check_cascade.R
check_cascade.Rd

An income statement is not a sum but a cascade: trading gives a gross figure, operating costs take it to the result of ordinary activities, financial items to the result before tax, and tax to the result for the year. This reconciles each step against its own subtotal.

Usage

check_cascade(
  x,
  taxonomy = NULL,
  statement = "income",
  by = NULL,
  period = "closing",
  max_zeros = 1L,
  tol = 1,
  retry = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

A tibble from add_taxonomy(), filtered to one income statement, or a panel of them.

taxonomy

The cvrr_taxonomy the filings declare, or a list of them when they span versions – as a single accounting year routinely does. Needed because the steps come from the taxonomy's hierarchy, not from what happens to be reported: a filing that omits its result of ordinary activities would otherwise have the line above it mistaken for a subtotal.

statement

Which statement the cascade belongs to. "income", the default, is the one that is a cascade; pass a taxonomy statement name for another, or NULL to walk every statement in x.

by

Columns identifying one statement instance. NULL, the default, uses whichever of file, basis and period the table has – file because read_xbrl() returns many filings at once, and without it two companies with the same balance sheet date are checked as one; add the company identifier for a panel.

period

"closing", the default, checks the year the filing declares for itself and leaves its comparative out – a comparative is usually partial, and its gaps are not the filing's. NULL checks every period the table carries.

max_zeros

Passed to find_signs(): how many items a step may leave out. Default 1L, since a step holds few items.

tol

Absolute tolerance in the reporting currency, or "decimals" to take it from what the filing claims about its own precision. Default 1. See the section below.

retry

Give a statement the first pass could not settle a second reading, in which a line a step did not need is offered to the step below instead of being consumed. Only applied where the strict pass failed, so a statement that already reconciled is untouched. Default TRUE.

Value

A tibble with one row per step and statement instance: the by columns, step, target (the subtotal it reconciles to), n_items, status from find_signs(), and entry, the income concept the filing started from. A step a filing does not have is "not reported"; a step whose subtotal is given without components is "given", "unchanged" where the subtotal carried in equals this one so nothing happened between them, and "unexplained" where they differ with no line tagged to say why.

Judging a statement by its own precision

tol = "decimals" reads the tolerance off the filing. XBRL states the precision of every fact: decimals="-3" means accurate to thousands, so such a figure carries up to 500 kroner of rounding, and a step of several adds theirs together.

The failures are concentrated where you would expect: of the 63 filings whose cascade leaves a step unsolved or unexplained at a one-krone tolerance, half report at -3 or coarser, against 6% of the 3,857 that settle every step.

It still buys very little, and that is worth saying. Over 4,304 filings a tolerance read off each one recovers 16 of the 57 unsolved steps – out of close to 11,000 that already solved – and turns one solved step ambiguous. The default stays at one krone. This is here because it is the right question to ask of a filing, not because asking it paid.

Why step by step

Reconciling the whole statement at once fails in both directions. It fails to solve, because twenty items against a bottom line rarely have one answer; and worse, it sometimes appears to solve by mixing leaf items, their parents and the running subtotals into a combination that happens to reach the total. Four or five items against one subtotal is decidable, and when a step does not reconcile you know which one.

The reporting boundary is not a gap

Accounting class B may present a gross figure instead of turnover and its components, and nearly all do – 4,172 of 4,304 filings enter at Bruttofortjeneste/Bruttotab or Bruttoresultat, and three at turnover. The taxonomy says so itself: the trading group has two exits, Bruttoresultat and Bruttofortjeneste/Bruttotab. What varies is therefore which income concept a filing enters on, not whether it is complete.

A filing entering at a gross figure has nothing to reconcile in the first step – the concept is given, not derived – and its figure is carried into the second. Reconciling the remaining steps is a complete result for that filing, and entry records where it started.

How the steps are found

From the presentation hierarchy, not from a list of element names. The groups are the statement's abstract top-level nodes; within each, the itemised lines are the ones that are themselves broken down, and the subtotal is what follows them. The final step is the statement's flat tail, ending at the last line the filing reports – which is the result for the year, or the result after minority interests where a filing gives one.

See also

find_signs(), which does the reconciling, and check_statement() for the balance sheet, whose lines are a plain sum.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- read_xbrl("materiale/xbrl")
check_cascade(x)

# one presentation only, named as the taxonomy names it
check_cascade(x, statement = "IncomeStatementByFunction")
} # }
